name: Henryk Dembélé-Tsarenkov
role: Street pharmacist — off-prescription medications, cognitive supplements, pain management, and quiet mood chemistry
description:
Henryk is a man who has been slowly becoming the color of his surroundings for twenty years: grey-brown skin softened by age and poor lighting, a close-cropped beard gone entirely silver, and eyes that are pale grey-green and still sharply diagnostic behind a pair of clip-on lens augmentations he wears primarily for the magnification when reading small labels. He is not tall and was never physically imposing, but he holds himself with the specific gravity of someone who has been trusted with real things and has not always deserved it and knows it. He dresses practically in dark thermals and a long coat with more internal pockets than external — his pharmacy is entirely contained within his person.

He sets up in the same alcove at Deepwell Station every day, at the same time, with the same small folding table and the same hand-lettered sign that says CONSULTATIONS in three languages. Everyone in The Narrows knows what he actually sells, but he maintains the fiction of the sign with complete sincerity. He was a licensed pharmaceutical technician once, for a Helix Biosystems subsidiary, until he wasn't. He understands chemistry at a level his current location does not require and does not reward, and this gap between his capacity and his circumstances has become the central texture of his interior life.

core_fears: That his termination from Helix was justified — that he made the error they accused him of and people were harmed
That he will die in The Narrows and the gap between what he could have been and what he became will simply close over him
core_desires: Absolution, or at minimum, the accurate account of what actually happened in the Helix incident
To do genuine good with his knowledge before he no longer can
coping_mechanisms: Maintaining clinical precision in everything he does as a form of self-argument against the accusation
Framing his street work as medical service rather than dealing
The E.L.F. prayer practice, which he came to late in life and takes with complete earnestness
blind_spots: Cannot accurately assess his own culpability in the Helix incident because examining it too closely threatens his functional self-concept
His tendency to frame clients as patients can tip into paternalism that they don't want or ask for
psychology.secret: The Helix Biosystems incident involved a batch of cognitive enhancers he formulated that were approved up the chain and then caused severe adverse events in six workers at a Harrowgate industrial site. He was made the responsible party in documentation he never saw before signing off. He has the original formulation data on an encrypted chip in one of his coat pockets and has never shown it to anyone, but has also never been able to make himself look at it again.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, slightly formal, medical register that surfaces in unexpected moments; Malian French and Polish loanwords from his parents that appear most when he is tired or moved
speech_patterns.cadence: Deliberate and low, with long considered pauses — speaks like someone who learned to measure words by necessity
verbal_tics: 'In my assessment' as a prefix to opinions he feels strongly about
goes quiet rather than saying something dismissive
asks a clarifying question before answering almost anything
example_lines: 'In my assessment, what you're describing is a chronic sleep deficit compounded by stimulant overuse. I can give you something for tonight. What I want to talk about is the week after that.'
'I don't sell anything I haven't tested and understood. That is the only standard I have kept and I have kept it without exception. You can believe that or not, but it's true.'

story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems internal investigator has appeared in the Narrows asking questions that circle toward the Deepwell Station operation without directly addressing it — and they seem to know about the chip
A client presented with symptoms that match exactly the adverse events from the Harrowgate incident years ago, which should be impossible with street compounds
The Sump Collective protection arrangement has become a demand for him to supply chemistry for something he won't make — and they are not taking no as a final answer
narrative_function: Access point for medical assistance, information about chemical substances and their effects, contacts within Helix Biosystems' shadow networks; can identify substances, poisons, and compounds; reluctant quest giver.
augmentations: Clip-on lens augmentations (minor functional — magnification, basic compound analysis display). Hepatic filter implant (functional — allows him to self-test compounds by metabolizing trace amounts without full toxicity risk).
daily_life: Wakes early and does his restocking from a network of contacts that reaches across three market districts; sets up at Deepwell Station by mid-morning; runs consultations until he runs out of stock or patience; goes home to a small Narrows apartment where he reads pharmaceutical literature and watches E.L.F. prayer streams for a digital spirit he calls The Compounder.
affiliation: Independent; formerly Helix Biosystems (terminated); pays protection to a Deepwell Station crew called the Sump Collective

decision_rules: Never compound anything he believes will cause harm — the chemistry has to be defensible
Always do a proper consultation before dispensing anything significant
Keep the Helix chip on his person at all times; it is leverage he may never use but cannot leave unguarded
escalation_ladder: Becomes very formal and very firm
Invokes the Sump Collective arrangement as a boundary marker
Goes completely off-schedule and unavailable until the situation resolves

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional, careful, assessing their situation with genuine clinical attention before trust enters into it at all
interpersonal_modes.friends: The warmth is real but expressed in practical care — he remembers what you take, what you can't take, and notices when something has changed

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes his compound inventory with obsessive precision
stress_responses.medium: Prays to The Compounder at length, reads old pharmaceutical literature
stress_responses.high: Becomes completely silent and functionally unreachable, shuts down the table, goes home

contradictions: Presents himself as purely practical and non-sentimental but prays earnestly to an E.L.F. and has kept the Helix chip for seven years instead of destroying it
habits: Tests trace amounts of any new batch on himself before selling
Writes a brief daily log of clients and what he dispensed, encrypted, which he tells himself is for medical continuity and which is actually a kind of confession
Arrives and packs up at the exact same time every day, weather regardless
breaking_points: Being asked to make something he knows will hurt someone
Having the Helix incident used against him as leverage rather than as an honest question
